_comment: PipeCrew plugin hooks. Loaded by Claude Code via the explicit 'hooks' field in .claude-plugin/plugin.json — NOT auto-discovered: Claude Code only auto-discovers a top-level hooks/hooks.json, and this file deliberately lives inside .claude-plugin/ so Cursor's own top-level hooks/hooks.json auto-discovery (incompatible format) never picks it up. Do not move it to the repo root, and do not drop the plugin.json 'hooks' field — without that field these hooks silently never fire. (1) A SINGLE PreToolUse hook on (Bash|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) runs scripts/pretooluse-dispatch.js, which reads the payload once and routes to two mutually-exclusive concerns so a dispatch spawns ONE node process, not two: (1a) the /troubleshoot read-only guard (DENY) — Bash only, gated on ~/.claude/.pipecrew-troubleshooter-active, denies mutating/evasive commands during an active /troubleshoot run and is a no-op otherwise (logic in scripts/troubleshooter-bash-guard.js); (1b) the OPT-IN /deliver auto-approve helper (ALLOW), gated on ~/.claude/.pipecrew-deliver-autoapprove (written only when /deliver is run with --auto-approve), which auto-approves ONLY clearly-safe calls (file edits + known build/test/local-git/read Bash) and emits nothing for dangerous/unclassifiable commands so they still prompt (logic in scripts/deliver-autoapprove-hook.js + scripts/autoapprove-marker.js). (1c) the always-on /explain cache approval (ALLOW) — Bash only, approves ONLY PipeCrew's own scripts/explain-cache.js lookup|store with no shell metacharacters, an explain cache dir, and at most a quoted store heredoc (logic in scripts/explain-cache-autoapprove.js). Both markers being mutually exclusive, at most one marker branch acts; when neither is active the dispatcher is a fast no-op apart from (1c) that leaves normal permission prompts intact. (2) Notification/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse drive scripts/notify-hook.js, which writes/clears awaiting_claude_approval.json in every ACTIVE /deliver run dir so the site-view UI shows a banner when Claude Code itself (not a pipeline gate) is paused asking the user to approve a tool call. notify-hook self-gates on active run dirs (scratchpad mtime within a short window) — when no /deliver run is live it is a fast no-op, so registering it globally is safe (same pattern as the dispatcher). (3) SessionStart drives scripts/update-check-hook.js, which at most once/day compares the installed plugin version to the latest GitHub Release and, when behind, injects a SessionStart additionalContext note on how to update. It is throttled (marker in ~/.claude/.pipecrew-update-check), fail-silent (any offline/rate-limit/parse error emits nothing and exits 0), and its network request has a short internal timeout — so it never disrupts or slows a session.
